newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Pennacchi corrects budget sums.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Pennacchi corrects budget sums.

text.p: Treasury Ministry undersecretary Laura Pennacchi said in a statement late on Tuesday she had never indicated 28 trillion lire as the likely total of deficit cuts needed in Italy's 1998 budget.
Her remarks came after she had indicated in an address to a seminar earlier in the day that Italy needed to cut its deficit by between 25 trillion and 28 trillion lire.
"With reference to reports from some media, I make clear that I never indicated 28 trillion lire as the total amount of the 1998 budget," Pennacchi said in a brief statement.
Other government officials had previously spoken of a deficit-cutting budget of 25 trillion lire for 1998.
The extent of the deficit cuts will be stated in the centre-left government's document of three-year rolling economic targets (DPEF), which political sources say the cabinet could approve on Friday.
Pennacchi had told the seminar earlier that the issue was how the deficit cuts should be achieved.
"Either you challenge the figure of 25 to 28 trillion lire, which in reality is more like 28, or you talk about how to achieve it," Pennacchi said.
Leaders of political parties that support the government met Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Monday night to discuss the DPEF, but failed to resolve differences over any welfare cuts in the measures.
Pennacchi said all the pro-government parties, including the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, agreed that the welfare state had to be reformed.
